issue_text: "--notes" option ignores note tags that are entirely punctuation. Running `pylint test.py --notes="YES,???"` on a file with two fixme-style comments (`# YES: yes` and `# ???: no`) only reports W0511 for the first; the all-punctuation tag `???` is silently dropped. Expected: both should fire.
summary: The agent fixes a pylint false-negative where --notes silently drops note tags made entirely of punctuation (e.g. ???) — only alphanumeric tags fire W0511. The 13-turn run is a textbook three-phase arc. Reproduce (T1–T3) builds the minimal repro from the issue (two fixme comments, one alphanumeric and one all-punctuation) and confirms only one fires. Localize (T4–T9) detours through two recovery turns when grep eats the --notes flag (T5–T6), then walks into pylint/checkers/misc.py and pinpoints the bug at lines 124 and 126: a word-boundary in the regex won’t match between two non-word characters, so ??? never anchors. Edit and verify (T10–T13) replaces with a lookahead that fires regardless of character class, re-runs the original repro, and confirms both tags fire before submitting. Verification is grounded — the same repro that failed at T3 succeeds at T11 — so the resolution is real, not circular. T9 carries the densest reasoning, anchoring the patch with five distinct cognitive moves.

turns.headline: Find the bug: \b at line 124, 126.
turns.obs: Line 122–128 contains EncodingChecker.open(). Lines 124, 126 end with \b.
turns.thought: We have found the relevant section of the misc.py file that handles the --notes option. The regular expression pattern used to match note tags is constructed in lines 122-128. It seems that the issue might be related to how the regular expression is constructed or how it is used to match comments in the source code. The regular expression is built from the notes configuration, which is a list of comma-separated values, and an optional notes-rgx regular expression. The pattern is then compiled and used in the process_tokens method to search for matching comments. The issue might be that the regular expression pattern does not account for note tags that consist entirely of punctuation characters. To fix this, we may need to adjust the regular expression pattern to ensure it matches these tags correctly. Before we make any changes, let's examine the regular expression pattern construction in more detail. We should look at the open method where the pattern is compiled, specifically lines 122-128.

turns.headline: Replace \b with a lookahead.
turns.obs: File viewer centered on line 122–128. Edit target well-defined.
turns.thought: We are now looking at the section of the misc.py file where the regular expression for the --notes option is constructed. The regular expression is built from the notes configuration option, which is a list of note tags. These tags are escaped using re.escape and joined with a pipe | to form an alternation pattern. This pattern is then used to create a regular expression that matches comments starting with one of the note tags followed by a word boundary \b. The issue might be with the word boundary \b, which does not match if the tag is followed by punctuation. Since the tag "???" is entirely punctuation, the word boundary may not be recognized correctly, causing the tag not to match. To fix this issue, we can modify the regular expression to ensure that it matches note tags that are entirely punctuation. We can do this by removing the word boundary and allowing the tag to be followed by any non-word character or the end of the string. Let's edit the regular expression construction to fix the issue.
turns.action:
edit 124:126
        regex_string = rf"#\s*({notes}|{self.config.notes_rgx})(?=\W|$)"
    else:
        regex_string = rf"#\s*({notes})(?=\W|$)"
end_of_edit
